messages:
elaine: Heads-up — Veridian reported 401s starting ~10:12 UTC after their API key rotation yesterday. Error rate ~15-25% depending on shard. Anyone seeing this?

sam: Yup, saw the spike on the support dashboard. Logs show a bunch of 'invalid_api_key' responses and sidecar errors like 'secret cache: token not found'. Most failing requests come from long-running workers.

devon: quick inventory: Vault shows the old key marked revoked, new key active. Our sidecar's secret cache uses lease_duration=3600 and we don't currently listen for revocation push notifications. If a pod started before rotation it might still hold the old key in memory until lease expiry.

elaine: Repro steps I used against a veridian pod:
```
# simulate a client using the old key
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <OLD_KEY>" \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' 

# response
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"key revoked"}
```

irene: fwiw I saw a transient KMS replication lag alert in us-west-2 earlier today but Veridian is in us-east-1 so doesn't look related here.

devon: TL;DR two vectors: 1) some deployments read the key from env var at pod start (so they never get the new key until restart). 2) sidecar caches secrets and only refreshes on lease expiry or explicit refresh — we don't proactively invalidate on explicit revocation.

sam: Customer rotated via Console -> Keys -> Rotate -> immediate revoke. They expected all backends to pick up new key immediately. We need to be explicit in docs and provide a better in-platform migration.

ops-bot: @here initiated a canary restart of 3 pods in namespace veridian-prod to validate the restart mitigation.

elaine: Mitigation options I gave the customer (fast):
```
# restart deployments to pick up new env var / re-pull secret
kubectl rollout restart deployment/veridian-api -n veridian-prod

# trigger sidecar refresh (internal admin endpoint) - requires admin token
curl -X POST https://<sidecar-host>/_admin/refresh-keys -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>"

# verify new key works
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <NEW_KEY>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
```

devon: Follow-ups I'm proposing: 
- add a sidecar feature to subscribe to Vault revocation events or poll sys/leases so we can proactively invalidate caches on revoke.
- implement a cluster-broadcast admin endpoint so an operator can trigger refresh across all pods without restart.
- update docs/Console UX to warn: "If your workload stores the key in env vars or long-lived cache, a rotation with immediate revoke requires rolling your fleet."

security: Escalating due to customer-visible auth failures and potential SLO breach. @devon please open an infra/security ticket with impact, repro logs, and proposed mitigation. Add priority P1/P2 suggestion.

devon: Opening INF-4823 now and attaching logs + repro. Short-term hotfix (admin broadcast endpoint + rollout orchestration) scoped to ~5 days; full sidecar event-subscribe solution ~2w.

elaine: Customer confirmed 401s dropped to ~0 after we rolled their deployment. They've asked for a short postmortem and explicit rotation guidance in the Console.

sam: I'll check billing side — ensure failed requests weren't billed incorrectly and confirm with billing ops.

ops-bot: incident recorded: incident/2027-03-05-keyRotationVeridian; timeline appended.

elaine: Summary: root cause = stale secret usage (env-var + sidecar cache) after immediate revocation. Immediate mitigation = restart pods or call admin refresh endpoint. Next actions = INF-4823, Console UX copy update, doc + runbook for rotation, and implement broadcast refresh / sidecar revocation watch. :white_check_mark:
